strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing interpretability in modern SSMs with principled mathematical framework grounded in orthogonal polynomials and classical dynamical systems theory
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 2, 3, 5) and comprehensive experimental details supporting reproducibility
Strong synthetic experiment design that cleanly isolates and demonstrates each proposed mechanism, with specialized variants achieving 100% accuracy on designed tasks (Table 1)
Novel unified framework combining several interpretability concepts; particularly elegant time-warping interpretation of Salience HiPPO (Eq. 3-5) and explicit OP-based associative memory structure
Honest discussion of interpretability vs. performance trade-offs with clear guidance for practitioners on when to use these variants
weaknesses: Severe performance degradation on realistic data: Associative Memory HiPPO achieves 20.41 PPL vs 5.54 for Mamba on WikiText-2 (269% gap), suggesting explicit mechanisms overfit to synthetic tasks and fundamentally fail to capture what modern SSMs learn

Limited real-world evaluation: only character-level language modeling tested; no evaluation on tasks where SSMs excel (long-range dependencies, sequence classification). Choice of WikiText-2 is suboptimal for SSM assessment

Systematic overfitting to toy problems: each variant evaluated primarily on synthetic tasks specifically designed to showcase that mechanism, with no intermediate-complexity benchmarks to test generalization

Unclear practical value proposition: practitioners will choose Mamba/S4D for performance; unclear who the intended audience is or why they should accept 20-36% performance degradation for interpretability gains

Technical concerns inadequately addressed: Volterra HiPPO's O(N^k) complexity not thoroughly analyzed; Salience HiPPO's scalar parameterization correlates only R²=0.38 with Mamba's vector-valued ∆t (Section F.3), suggesting important structure is missed; Associative Memory's continuous addressing fundamentally mismatched to discrete token prediction

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem of making SSM memory mechanisms explicit and interpretable
Strong mathematical foundations with elegant insights (time-warping interpretation of Salience HiPPO, predictive memory geometry analysis)
Excellent experimental design for isolating specific mechanisms through well-motivated synthetic tasks (selective copying, associative recall, variable-horizon reconstruction)
Effective visualizations that compellingly demonstrate interpretability (Figures 2, 3, 5 clearly show induced history measures and learned representations)
Unified framework showing five distinct capabilities fit within single interpretable polynomial framework
Rigorous derivations and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Honest acknowledgment of limitations and performance-interpretability tradeoffs
weaknesses: Severe performance degradation on realistic tasks: Vanilla HiPPO + MLP achieves 6.80 PPL vs. Mamba's 5.54 PPL (23% gap), and specialized variants (Associative Memory: 20.41 PPL, Salience: 7.52 PPL) fail catastrophically on language modeling despite perfect performance on synthetic tasks
Insufficient investigation of why synthetic performance doesn't transfer to natural tasks or how to bridge this gap
Task-specific brittleness: mechanisms designed for specific capabilities (e.g., Associative Memory for key-value binding) fail fundamentally on different tasks, questioning their generality
Limited practical guidance on when interpretability gains justify significant performance costs
Computational overhead underexplored: Volterra HiPPO grows as O(N^k); Multiscale HiPPO uses O(NM²); no wall-clock timing or analysis of cost-benefit tradeoffs
No end-to-end demonstration on realistic task where interpretability demonstrably helps practitioners (e.g., scientific computing, legal document analysis)
Baseline comparisons concern: single-layer models perform surprisingly poorly; two-layer S4D reaches 96.9% on selective copying, much closer to Salience HiPPO's 100%
Missing ablations: no sensitivity analysis for polynomial coefficient dimension N, initialization effects, or convergence properties
Language modeling section (3.6) too brief given the poor and unexpected results—deserves deeper investigation into whether mechanisms are fundamentally unsuitable
